key_insight: SAMRI-3D adapts SAM2 to 3D MRI segmentation by adding global volume tokens and MRI-specific tuning, improving accuracy while preserving strong generalization to unseen datasets.
clinical_relevance: This could help automate MRI segmentation more reliably across many anatomical regions and scan types, especially where slice-by-slice boundaries are hard to see.
method: Built SAMRI-3D, an MRI-only benchmark with 10,392 volumes from 34 datasets and seen/unseen splits.
Froze the image encoder and fine-tuned only the decoder and memory modules for efficient adaptation.
Added Global Volume Tokens trained with a TSDF reconstruction objective to capture whole-volume context; the TSDF loss is removed at inference.
evidence_signal: On 34 datasets, mean Dice improved from 0.58 for zero-shot SAM2 to 0.76 with light fine-tuning, and the full SAMRI-3D model reached 0.78 with no drop on held-out datasets.
watch_item: The approach depends on specialized MRI benchmark training and validation, so performance may vary when transferred to new scanners, protocols, or pathology mixes without further evaluation.
paper_title: SAMRI-3D: Adapting SAM2 for 3D MRI Segmentation with Global Volume Tokens
